e: The European Union forms a new support mission for Lebanon.
President Aoun orders security chiefs to stay away from the memorial ceremony for Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah.
A hunger strike is initiated by hundreds of prisoners at Roumieh Prison due to the stalled implementation of a sweeping amnesty law.
A relative of former Syrian president Bashar al-Assad is arrested in Lebanon.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announces sanctions on the Hezbollah-affiliated Al-Qard Al-Hasan Association.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announces that five Lebanese civilians were released by Israel in exchange for information on Jewish remains in Lebanon.
The US imposes sanctions against Hezbollah, citing its actions on behalf of the Government of Iran.
Prime Minister Nawaf Salam states that hackers deleted posts condemning Israeli attacks and occupation.
A contentious sweeping amnesty law for prisoners and fugitives is passed by Parliament.
Parliament abolishes the death penalty, a first for the Arab world, over opposition from Hezbollah's parliamentary caucus.

Lebanon arrests a Syrian soldier who commanded the 17th Division under former President Bashar al-Assad for alleged crimes during the Syrian civil war. Lebanon later decides to hand over him to Syria after questioning.
Lebanon and Israel agree on a shortlist of states that could send forces to verify Hezbollah disarmament.
The IDF stated that roughly 15 Israelis, mostly girls, infiltrated the Lebanese border before returning to Israel.
Lebanon arrests an ex-Palestinian envoy on PA corruption charges.

Over a dozen Lebanese lawyers file a complaint against a banker who met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, stating that Lebanon's laws prohibit its citizens from contacting Israelis as the two nations have in a state of war since Israel's establishment in 1948.
Lebanon detains a person suspected of transferring fund to Islamic State in Syria.
UNIFIL soldiers neutralize four tons of explosives apparently left by Israel in Houla.
The castles of Mount Amel are designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Lebanon announces that the Lebanese army started deploying in Zawtar al-Gharbiyah following Israeli withdrawal from the town in accordance with the 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire.
US President Donald Trump orders to allow direct US–Lebanon flights.
The US announces that Israel handed over sections of its buffer zone in southern Lebanon to Lebanese control as part of the 2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire.
The US State Department states that Israel agreed to withdraw from pilot zones in southern Lebanon.
Lebanon detains a person close to Hezbollah on suspicion of spying for Israel.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announces a framework deal between Israel and Lebanon that aims to achieve "lasting peace and security" through US mediation. The agreement asks for a cease-fire, with Hezbollah agreeing to terminate all hostilities and withdraw from southern Lebanon. Hezbollah later rejects it.
President Trump announces a renewed ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

Pakistan, the primary mediator, states that both the United States and Iran declared the "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" as part of the agreement to end the 2026 Iran war. Israel states that its forces will remain in Lebanon.

Israel announces that it killed Ali Musa Daqduq, a senior Hezbollah commander responsible for the Karbala provincial headquarters raid that killed five American soldiers during the Iraq War in a strike in southern Lebanon over the weekend.
Saudi Arabia lifts a ban on imports from Lebanon that had been in place since 2021.

Lebanese ⁠state media says that an Israeli strike in the southern suburbs of Beirut kills two people and injures 11 others. The IDF says that it targeted Hezbollah infrastructure after the group fired towards northern Israel.
Rene Mouawad Airport in Qleiat is inaugurated in a ceremony led by prime minister Nawaf Salam.
A Serbian peacekeeper is killed while two others are injured in a strike on a UNIFIL base in southern Lebanon.
Hezbollah rejects the truce deal announced the previous day and demands a comprehensive truce and full withdrawal of Israel from Lebanon.
Israel and Lebanon agree to renew the ceasefire mediated by the US, and to establish "pilot zones".
Israel agrees not to hit Beirut's southern suburbs, and Hezbollah agrees not to attack Israel as part of a US proposal, with the cease-fire framework to be expanded to include entire Lebanon.
An Israeli airstrike on a residential building in Sir el Gharbiyeh kills at least 11 people and injures six.
Six people are killed and six more injured in an Israeli airstrike in Deir Qanoun an-Naher. Two paramedics are among the fatalities, while three more are injured.
A paramedic is killed and four more are injured in two separate Israeli airstrikes in Tyre District.
Israeli airstrikes kill at least eight people in Ad-Doueir, Tibnin, Burj el-Shamali, and Shebaa.
Israeli airstrikes kill 19 people and injure 34 in Nabatieh District and Tyre District.
